verses.1:1: Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy, to the church of the Thessalonians in God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:2: Grace to you and peace. We always give thanks to God for all of you, mentioning you in our prayers without interruption,
verses.1:3: mindful of the work of your faith, and of labor, and of love, and of the endurance of the hope of our Lord Jesus Christ before our God and Father,
verses.1:4: knowing, brothers loved by God, your election,
verses.1:5: because our gospel did not come to you in speech alone, but also in power, and in the Holy Spirit, and in much fullness, just as you know what sort of men we were among you for your sake.
verses.1:6: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, receiving the word in much affliction, with joy of the Holy Spirit,
verses.1:7: so that you became a pattern to all who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
verses.1:8: For from you the word of the Lord has been spread widely, not only in Macedonia and in Achaia, but also in every place your faith, which is toward God, has gone out, so that it is not necessary for us to say anything.
verses.1:9: For they themselves report about us what kind of entrance we had to you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,
verses.1:10: and to wait for His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead, Jesus, who has rescued us from the coming wrath.
verses.2:1: For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance to you, that it was not in vain;
verses.2:2: but having suffered beforehand and been subjected to mistreatment, as you know, in Philippi, we had confidence in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much anxiety.
verses.2:3: For our exhortation is not from error, nor from impurity, nor in deceit,
verses.2:4: but just as we were approved by God so that the gospel might be entrusted to us, so we speak, not as pleasing people, but God, who tests our hearts.
verses.2:5: For neither at any time were we found in speech of flattery, as you know, nor in a pretext for greed (God is witness),
verses.2:6: nor seeking glory from people, either from you or from others.
verses.2:7: Although we could have been a burden to you as apostles of Christ, yet we became little children in your midst, just as a nursing mother cherishes her own children.
verses.2:8: Longing for you in this way, we eagerly wanted to impart to you not only the gospel of God, but also our souls, because you became most dear to us.
verses.2:9: For you are mindful, brothers, of our labor and weariness: working night and day, so that we would not burden any of you, we proclaimed the gospel of God among you.
verses.2:10: You are witnesses, and so is God, how holy, and just, and without blame we were toward you who have believed,
verses.2:11: just as you know how, with each one of you, like a father with his own children,
verses.2:12: imploring you and comforting you, we testified that you should walk worthy of God, who called you into His own kingdom and glory.
verses.2:13: For this reason we also give thanks to God without interruption, because when you received from us the word of the hearing of God, you received it not as a word of human beings, but, as it truly is, the word of God, who works in you who have believed.
verses.2:14: For you became imitators, brothers, of the churches of God that are in Judea in Christ Jesus, because you also suffered the same things from your fellow countrymen, just as they also did from the Jews,
verses.2:15: who killed both the Lord Jesus and the prophets, and persecuted us, and do not please God, and oppose all people,
verses.2:16: forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles so that they may be saved, so that they always fill up their sins; for the wrath of God has come upon them to the very end.
verses.2:17: But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for the space of an hour, in sight, not in heart, hastened all the more to see your face with much longing,
verses.2:18: because we wanted to come to you, indeed I, Paul, both once and again; yet Satan hindered us.
verses.2:19: For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of glory? Is it not you, before our Lord Jesus Christ at His coming?
verses.2:20: For you are our glory and joy.
verses.3:1: Therefore, when we could endure it no longer, it seemed good to us to remain in Athens alone,
verses.3:2: and we sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and to exhort you concerning your faith,
verses.3:3: so that no one may be shaken in these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we have been appointed for this.
verses.3:4: For even when we were with you, we kept telling you beforehand that we would suffer afflictions, just as indeed happened, and you know.
verses.3:5: For this reason I also, enduring it no longer, sent to learn about your faith, for fear that perhaps the one who tempts might have tempted you, and our labor might become in vain.
verses.3:6: But now that Timothy has come to us from you and reported to us your faith and love, and that you always have a good memory of us, longing to see us just as we also long to see you,
verses.3:7: for this reason we have been comforted, brothers, in you, in all our distress and affliction, through your faith,
verses.3:8: because now we live, if you stand in the Lord.
verses.3:9: For what thanksgiving can we render back to God for you in all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,
verses.3:10: praying all the more night and day that we may see your face and complete those things that are lacking in your faith?
verses.3:11: Now may our God and Father Himself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you.
verses.3:12: And may the Lord multiply you and make your love abound toward one another and toward all, just as we also do toward you,
verses.3:13: to strengthen your hearts without blame in holiness before our God and Father, at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all His saints. Amen.
verses.4:1: Furthermore, then, brothers, we ask and implore you in the Lord Jesus that, just as you received from us how you ought to walk and to please God, so also you should walk, in order that you may abound even more.
verses.4:2: For you know what commands I gave you through the Lord Jesus.
verses.4:3: For this is God's will, your sanctification: that you abstain from fornication,
verses.4:4: that each one of you know how to possess his own vessel in sanctification and honor,
verses.4:5: not in the passion of desire, as the Gentiles also do, who do not know God,
verses.4:6: and that no one transgress or defraud his brother in a matter, because the Lord is an avenger concerning all these things, just as we told you beforehand and bore witness.
verses.4:7: For God did not call us to impurity, but to sanctification.
verses.4:8: Therefore, the one who spurns these things does not spurn man, but God, who also gave His Holy Spirit in us.
verses.4:9: Now concerning brotherly love, we have no need to write to you, for you yourselves have learned from God to love one another.
verses.4:10: Indeed, you do this toward all the brothers throughout all of Macedonia. Yet we ask you, brothers, that you abound even more,
verses.4:11: and strive to be quiet, and attend to your own business, and work with your hands, just as we commanded you,
verses.4:12: and that you walk honorably toward those who are outside, and desire nothing from anyone.
verses.4:13: Now we do not want you to be unaware, brothers, concerning those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve as the rest also do, who have no hope.
verses.4:14: For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with Him those who have fallen asleep through Jesus.
verses.4:15: For we say this to you in the word of the Lord, that we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, will not precede those who have fallen asleep.
verses.4:16: Because the Lord Himself will descend from heaven with a command, and with the voice of an archangel, and with the trumpet of God; and the dead who are in Christ will rise first.
verses.4:17: Afterward we who are alive, who are left, will be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet Christ in the air; and thus we will always be with the Lord.
verses.4:18: So then, comfort one another with these words.
verses.5:1: Now concerning the times and the moments, brothers, you have no need for us to write to you.
verses.5:2: For you yourselves know thoroughly that, just like a thief in the night, so the day of the Lord will come.
verses.5:3: For when they say, "Peace and security," then sudden destruction will come upon them, like pain upon a woman with child, and they will not escape.
verses.5:4: But you, brothers, are not in darkness, for that day to overtake you like a thief.
verses.5:5: For all of you are sons of light and sons of the day; we are not of the night, nor of darkness.
verses.5:6: Therefore, let us not sleep as the rest also do, but let us stay awake and be sober.
verses.5:7: For those who sleep, sleep at night; and those who are drunk, are drunk at night.
verses.5:8: But let us who are of the day be sober, wearing the breastplate of faith and love, and as a helmet the hope of salvation,
verses.5:9: because God did not appoint us to wrath, but to the obtaining of salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,
verses.5:10: who died for us, so that whether we stay awake or sleep, we may live together with Him.
verses.5:11: For this reason, comfort one another and build each other up, just as you are also doing.
verses.5:12: Now we ask you, brothers, that you recognize those who labor among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you,
verses.5:13: that you hold them more abundantly in love because of their work. Have peace with them.
verses.5:14: And we ask you, brothers: reprove the unruly, comfort the fainthearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.
verses.5:15: See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone, but always pursue what is good toward one another and toward all.
verses.5:18: Give thanks in all things, for this is God's will in Christ Jesus concerning all of you.
verses.5:21: But test all things; hold fast to what is good.
verses.5:23: Now may the God of peace Himself sanctify you in every respect, so that your whole spirit, and soul, and body may be kept without blame at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.5:24: Faithful is He who called you, who will also do it.
verses.5:26: Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.
verses.5:27: I put you under oath by the Lord that this letter be read to all the holy brothers.
verses.5:28: May the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

notes.1:2: In the Clementine Vulgate, 'Grace to you and peace' (Gratia vobis, et pax) opens verse 2 rather than closing verse 1, and 'without interruption' (sine intermissione) closes verse 2 rather than beginning verse 3 as in modern Greek editions.
notes.1:3: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'et laboris, et caritatis' ('and of labor, and of love'), coordinating the two nouns with 'et' rather than rendering the Greek genitive phrase 'labor of love.'
notes.1:5: Vulgate 'in plenitudine multa' literally means 'in much fullness,' corresponding to the Greek phrase for 'in full conviction' or 'full assurance.'
notes.1:10: Vulgate 'eripuit' is perfect tense ('has rescued'), whereas the Greek text uses a present participle ('who rescues/delivers').
notes.2:2: Vulgate 'in multa sollicitudine' literally means 'in much anxiety' (or 'anxious concern'), differing in nuance from the Greek 'in much conflict/struggle.'
notes.2:7: Vulgate 'parvuli' ('little children') follows the Greek textual variant 'nepioi' ('infants/little children') rather than 'epioi' ('gentle').
notes.2:13: Vulgate 'verbum auditus Dei' ('the word of the hearing of God') reproduces the Greek genitive idiom meaning 'the message of God that you heard.' In addition, the masculine relative pronoun 'qui' ('who works') agrees grammatically with 'Dei' ('God') rather than with neuter 'verbum' ('word').
notes.2:19: Vulgate 'corona gloriae' reads 'crown of glory,' rendering the Greek phrase 'crown of boasting/exultation.'
notes.3:2: Vulgate 'ministrum Dei' ('minister of God') follows the Greek textual variant 'diakonon tou theou' rather than 'synergon tou theou' ('co-worker of God').
notes.3:12: Vulgate 'Vos ... multiplicet, et abundare faciat caritatem vestram' ('multiply you and make your love abound') places 'your love' in the accusative as the object of 'make abound,' whereas the Greek uses a dative ('make you increase and abound in love').
notes.3:13: The Clementine Vulgate concludes verse 13 with 'Amen,' agreeing with the majority Greek textual tradition against the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.4:1: The Vulgate uses the subjunctive "sic et ambuletis" ("so also you should walk") as part of the exhortation, whereas critical Greek texts read an indicative ("just as you are walking").
notes.4:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads first-person singular "dederim" ("I gave"), whereas Greek manuscripts read the plural ("we gave").
notes.4:4: Literally "possess his own vessel" ("vas suum possidere"); Latin "possidere" ("possess, control") translates Greek ktasthai ("acquire, take"), and "vessel" is variously understood as one's own body or one's wife.
notes.4:8: The Vulgate includes "haec" ("these things"), uses the past tense "dedit" ("gave"), and reads first-person "in nobis" ("in us"), whereas critical Greek texts omit "these things," use a present participle ("gives"), and read second-person "to you."
notes.4:17: The Vulgate reads "obviam Christo" ("to meet Christ"), whereas standard Greek texts read "to meet the Lord."
notes.5:13: The Vulgate reads "pacem habete cum eis" ("Have peace with them," referring to the leaders), whereas critical Greek texts read "be at peace among yourselves."
notes.5:18: The Vulgate reads "in omnibus vobis" ("concerning all of you"), including "omnibus" ("all") where standard Greek texts read simply "for you."
notes.5:22: Latin "specie mala" uses an adjective ("evil appearance" or "evil form") rather than a genitive; "species" carries both the sense of outward "appearance" and that of "form" or "kind."
notes.5:23: The Vulgate links the second clause with "ut" ("so that ... may be kept") as a purpose or result clause rather than a second coordinate wish, and "per omnia" literally means "through all things" or "in every respect."
notes.5:27: The Vulgate includes "sanctis" ("holy") in "omnibus sanctis fratribus" ("all the holy brothers"), and v. 28 concludes with "Amen," reflecting the traditional Vulgate text rather than the shorter critical Greek text.
